newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end week with sharp losses.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end week with sharp losses.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures posted sharp losses in brisk trade as technical worries overwhelmed the market.
"I think there has been a huge change in psychology (and) people aren't afraid to sell this stuff," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "The horse is out of the barn."
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures fell as low as 898.05, the lowest price in more than 6-1/2 weeks.
"Once the Dow started coming off, we set off a whole bunch of stops and all the houses started selling them down," another S&P trader said of Friday's late action.

The late push lower was swift and violent, yanking September S&Ps through myriad support levels. Traders said a sluggish dollar and earnings warnings from Gillette planted the bearish seed early in the day, with technical worries taking over from there.
Traders noted a thicket of sell-stops at 915.50.
"There was just lots of selling," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
Several said they expect more selling early Monday.
"We'll see 872.00 if we really get crazy Monday," another trader said. "That's roughly 10 percent from the top."
That trader noted a lack of any interest on the buy side and also noted options expiration-related weakness.
August S&P 500 options expired Thursday and settled early Friday, while S&P 100 options went off the board Friday and settle Saturday.
"It's typical expiration volatility," an options trader said. "It seems to be a little program-related -- the unwinding of some buy programs that hit the floor about a month ago," he said.
September S&P 500 futures volume was estimated at 75,000 contracts.
The futures trader said the volume estimate, shown on Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards, may be overstated slightly.
"And on a power move like that, I want to see over 100,000 contracts traded," the trader said. "I'm not ready to throw in the towel yet."

At the close, September S&P 500s fell 29.25 to 898.80, Midcap 400s lost 2.80 to 308.90, Russell 2000 dropped 3.75 to 410.50, Value Lines dropped 15.25 pts to 822.00, NYSE Composite fell 13.90 to 467.60, NASDAQ lost 39.00 to 1072.50, and Nikkei fell 365.0 to 19,030.00.
